correctness.rationale: At a fixed index, normalizing the positive modal contributions and putting a=1-lambda gives Delta e=-e E[a] and Delta^2 e=e E[a^2], so the Aitken residual ratio is exactly Var(a)/E[a^2]. The bounded-variable inequality E[a^2]<=(m+M)E[a]-mM reduces the problem to a one-variable maximization with exact maximum ((M-m)/(M+m))^2. Equality conditions force endpoint support and the stated weights. The exact-rational verifier reproduces the identity and sharp witness.

value.rationale: Positive mixtures of decaying exponentials are a natural error model for self-adjoint positive stationary iterations and scalar spectral observables. The theorem gives a sign-safe, sharp finite-index guarantee for a classical three-point accelerator and quantifies exactly when its three inputs beat simply taking two further raw iterations. The endpoint equality case makes the bound directly usable as a worst-case benchmark.
